entities.summary: Ann Bishop was a British biologist from Girton College at the University of Cambridge and a Fellow of the Royal Society, one of the few female Fellows of the Royal Society. She was born in Manchester but stayed at Cambridge for the vast majority of her professional life. Her specialties were protozoology and parasitology; early work with ciliate parasites, including the one responsible for blackhead disease in the domesticated turkey, lay the groundwork for her later research. While working towards her doctorate, Bishop studied parasitic amoebae and examined potential chemotherapies for the treatment of amoebic diseases including amoebic dysentery.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ann Bishop's pioneering research on protozoology and parasitology led to a better understanding of blackhead disease in domesticated turkeys, contributing to advancements in veterinary medicine. Her work also laid the groundwork for potential chemotherapies against amoebic diseases.
